utility.notes: The City of Industry is confirmed to be within SCE's distribution service territory.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own homepage states it serves '38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties' and names each one individually via its site's community directory; City of Industry is not among the named communities. No other Los Angeles/Ventura County CCA serving City of Industry was found, so Southern California Edison (SCE) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: Los Angeles County Department of Public Works, Building and Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: The City of Industry does not operate its own building department; per the city's own site, all building, electrical, mechanical, and plumbing permits — including solar — are issued by LA County Building & Safety, operating out of a satellite office within City of Industry.

permit_url.notes: The fetched page confirms the contract-city arrangement with LA County and the online BSOP portal, but did not itemize solar-specific requirements, fees, or timelines.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this dataset.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across SCE's entire distribution territory, which includes City of Industry/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.
